LESSON: COMPOSITION OF AIR

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Matter
Topic 2.2: Composition of Air
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Composition of Air, part of Matter in Grade 6 SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How does air pollution affect the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the meaning air and its constituent,

2. draw a pie chart showing percentage composition of components of air,

3. carry out activity to investigate the presence of oxygen in air collaboratively (use a burning candle),

4. discuss with peers the uses of the different components of air,

5. brainstorm on the meaning of air pollution,

6. explore the school and neighbourhood to identify air pollutants,

7. discuss with peers the effects of air pollution on the environment,

8. identify and discuss methods of reducing air pollution,

9. use digital or print media to search for more information on the effects of air pollution. Note: observe safety precautions in air-

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the meaning air and its constituent,
2. draw a pie chart showing percentage composition of components of air,
3. carry out activity to investigate the presence of oxygen in air collaboratively (use a burning candle),
4. discuss with peers the uses of the different components of air,
5. brainstorm on the meaning of air pollution,
6. explore the school and neighbourhood to identify air pollutants,
7. discuss with peers the effects of air pollution on the environment,
8. identify and discuss methods of reducing air pollution,
9. use digital or print media to search for more information on the effects of air pollution. Note: observe safety precautions in air-

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Composition of Air together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: The learner relates concept of environmental conservation as they discuss on air pollutants and come up with ways

of reducing air pollution in the environment.

● Learning to learn: The learner learns new skills of controlling air pollutants as they explore the school and neighbourhood to

identify air pollutants.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner observes safety precautions in an air-polluted environment as they identify and discuss methods of

reducing air pollution.

● Patriotism: The learner serves the community by making posters on common air pollutants, dangers of air pollution and ways of

controlling air pollution to educate members of the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Socio-economic and environmental issues (Environmental education and climate change): The learner practises ways of

environmental conservation as they identify and discuss methods of reducing air pollution.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

Mathematics: The learner uses mathematical skills to draw a pie chart showing the percentage composition of components of air.
